transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Michael Turner (Ember - Head of ML), Sofia Reyes (Ember - CTO), Jordan Lee (Ember - DevOps)

Summary (auto): 6-week pilot scoped; primary goals are below target latency (<=150ms p50 on critical routes), cost per 1k requests to be under $X (ballpark), and model quality >= current in-house baseline for classification. Access plan: SSO, sample data upload to a staging bucket, and limited VPN/VPC egress for private deployment if needed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex from Redwood, Priya from the SE team.
[00:08] Michael Turner: Michael here. Hey.
[00:10] Sofia Reyes: Hi, Sofia on the call.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Jordan, DevOps.
[00:15] Alex Kim: Cool. Goal today is to scope a POC timeline and milestones so you can get a sense for effort and what success looks like. Priya jump in on the technical framing.
[00:25] Priya Desai: Yeah hi all. Quick overview: shows of hands — you're primarily running a document classification + summarization pipeline, right Michael?
[00:33] Michael Turner: Yep, that's correct. We process internal statements, customer support tickets and some regulatory docs. Throughput peaks around 120 req/s during batch windows, but real-time routes are closer to 8-12 rps.
[00:45] Priya Desai: Got it. For the POC we typically mirror a production slice — can you confirm average seq lengths and token distribution?
[00:53] Michael Turner: Most docs are 500-1,200 tokens; summaries are short, 60-120 tokens. There's a long tail of bigger regulatory PDFs.
[01:04] Priya Desai: Helpful. So scope wise we'll do two tracks: hosted Redwood API for quick validation and optional Dedicated/Private test to evaluate latency/cost tradeoffs and any VPC constraints.
[01:15] Sofia Reyes: For us security is a hard requirement — we need SOC 2 details, SSO, audit logs, and the option for a private deployment if data residency or egress becomes an issue.
[01:27] Alex Kim: Totally, we can provide SOC 2 docs and the audit log examples; private deployment is part of Redwood Private if we need to go that route. We'll note that as a contingency.
[01:35] Jordan Lee: Practically we'll need an onboarding checklist — access to a staging bucket, service account keys, and SAML metadata. Also network egress rules for a private connector.
[01:45] Priya Desai: We'll send an access checklist. On the performance side: what's your p50/p95 SLO target for the real-time route?
[01:52] Michael Turner: Ideally p50 < 150ms, p95 under 600ms for the user-facing path. If that forces too much cost we can discuss relaxations but that's the business ask.
[02:03] Priya Desai: That's helpful. For costs we need the expected token per request — you said 500-1200 tokens input, 60-120 output, so per request ~700-1300 tokens. Also is batching acceptable for some routes?
[02:15] Michael Turner: For background processing yes; for UX-critical flows no. So we need to measure both steady-state throughput and low-latency single-request latency.
[02:23] Alex Kim: OK we'll propose a benchmark matrix: single-request latency test, continuous throughput test at 120rps with representative token sizes, and quality comparison vs your in-house model on the classification tasks.
[02:35] Sofia Reyes: On quality, what's the plan for evaluation? We'll need exact metrics — precision/recall/F1, and a small human evaluation for summarization.
[02:43] Priya Desai: We'll run an eval harness — you provide labeled holdout and a small human review set (20-30 samples) for summarization. We'll return detailed metrics and examples.
[02:52] Michael Turner: Sounds good. Timeline? You said 6 weeks earlier — can you walk through milestones?
[02:58] Alex Kim: Sure. Proposed 6-week plan: Week 0 (kickoff + access/setup), Week 1-2 (baseline runs + initial benchmarks), Week 3 (mid-point review + adjustments), Week 4-5 (final runs + optimizations), Week 6 (exec readout and decision).
[03:15] Alex Kim: Kickoff we confirm success criteria, SOW, and grant access. Mid-point review we'll share preliminary benchmarks and any blockers. Exec readout we'll present final results and recommended next steps.
[03:26] Jordan Lee: For access are you expecting us to open firewall rules or can we use a private connector?
[03:31] Priya Desai: Either works. For Hosted API it's usually SAML + secure upload to a staging bucket. For Private, we need a private connector or VPC peering. We'll provide both options in the checklist.
[03:42] Sofia Reyes: A couple of things — we might require data redaction before sending samples; also compliance needs KMS integration for keys.
[03:49] Priya Desai: We support KMS/HSM integrations on Private; for hosted flows we can discuss tokenization and prefix-only caching options. We'll also show how audit logs capture request metadata.
[03:58] Michael Turner: On success criteria: 1) latency targets met on low-latency routes, 2) classification F1 >= our baseline +/- 2 points, 3) cost per 1k requests improved or at parity with a path to cost reduction, and 4) secure access and auditability.
[04:15] Alex Kim: Good explicit success criteria — we'll put those in the SOW. Any constraints on running benchmarks in your cloud account?
[04:22] Jordan Lee: We're on GCP, we can provide a project and service account with restricted permissions. Need to coordinate IAM roles.
[04:29] Priya Desai: Perfect. We'll need a staging bucket, sample dataset upload instructions, and an IP allowlist if you prefer hosted tests to come from a fixed Redwood egress IP range.
[04:40] Michael Turner: Regarding benchmark numbers — can Redwood share a sample benchmark sheet and the exact test harness you use?
[04:46] Alex Kim: Yes — we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and the harness link. It includes scripts for single-request latency, concurrent throughput, and quality evaluation.
[04:54] Sofia Reyes: What's the expected Redwood side effort? SE hours, any infra work?
[05:00] Alex Kim: For the 6-week POC, typical Redwood SE involvement is about 8-12 hours/week early, tapering later. We'll also include provisioning for a dedicated engineer for the kick-off and mid-point reviews. Any dedicated deployment (Private) will add provisioning time (up to 1-2 weeks extra for networking and KMS setup).
[05:18] Priya Desai: I'll list out the technical tasks in the runbook: onboarding, data ingest, test harness runs, and metric collection. For dedicated/private we'll include extra checklist items.
[05:27] Michael Turner: Budget — we need an estimate for a pilot cost. We can discuss contract terms after the POC but ballpark numbers help for internal approvals.
[05:35] Alex Kim: We'll include a pricing sheet in the SOW — two tracks: hosted trial credit estimate and Dedicated pilot pricing with reserved capacity for the test window.
[05:44] Jordan Lee: One question: do you support quantized models to reduce cost? We run some 8-bit quantized clusters in-house.
[05:50] Priya Desai: Redwood Optimize includes model/quantization recommendations. For the POC we'll test a quantized variant if acceptable and measure quality delta. We'll log per-token latency and memory.
[06:03] Sofia Reyes: For exec readout can you provide an executive one-pager with clear recommendations and cost delta?
[06:09] Alex Kim: Absolutely, the final deliverable will be a slide deck and one-pager summarizing benchmarks, costs, and recommended next steps.
[06:17] Michael Turner: OK so concrete asks from us: share sample data + baseline model outputs, provide SSO metadata, and confirm timeline availability for kickoff week of Oct 12.
[06:28] Alex Kim: Yep I'll add that to the action items. We'll send SOW and checklist by Oct 4.
[06:33] Priya Desai: Quick technical note — for the throughput test we should cap batch sizes to match your production preprocessor; otherwise results won't be representative.
[06:41] Michael Turner: We'll provide preprocessor details and sample pre-batched records.
[06:45] Alex Kim: Anything else on the success criteria?
[06:48] Sofia Reyes: Also need proof of data residency controls — where logs are stored and retention.
[06:53] Priya Desai: We'll include log retention settings and the ability to export audit logs to your GCP project.
[06:59] Jordan Lee: On credentials — we'd prefer short-lived service account keys or workload identity; avoid long-lived keys if possible.
[07:06] Priya Desai: Agreed. We'll document recommended practices and can support Workload Identity Federation.
[07:13] Alex Kim: Great. Let's quickly walk through the milestone dates and owners: Kickoff (week of 2026-10-12) — Redwood: Alex/Priya to run; Ember: Michael/Sofia to provide access. Access/setup complete by 2026-10-16. Baseline runs complete by 2026-10-23. Mid-point review 2026-10-26. Final runs by 2026-10-30. Exec readout 2026-11-02. Does that align with your expectations?
[07:37] Michael Turner: That timeline looks tight but workable. We'll flag any internal calendar conflicts, but let's tentatively lock those dates.
[07:44] Sofia Reyes: Works for me.
[07:46] Jordan Lee: Works.
[07:47] Alex Kim: Great. Any risks we should call out?
[07:50] Priya Desai: Potential risks: sample data not representative, network/VPC provisioning delays, and model quality gaps with quantized variants. We'll note mitigations: early sample vetting, pre-provisioned network templates, and quality gates at mid-point.
[08:03] Michael Turner: Sounds reasonable.
[08:06] Alex Kim: Recap of next steps: Alex send SOW + pricing by 2026-10-04, Priya send onboarding checklist by 2026-10-03, Ember to provide sample data + SSO info by 2026-10-06, tentatively schedule kickoff week of 2026-10-12.
[08:21] Priya Desai: I'll attach the benchmark harness and an example spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[08:26] Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with calendar invites and the doc links.
[08:30] Michael Turner: Thanks all. Looking forward.
[08:32] Sofia Reyes: Thanks.
[08:33] Jordan Lee: Thanks.
[45:00] End of recording.
